problems.title: Formatting one line inside a multiline literal changes its value
problems.summary: A format range can put a marker inside a triple-quoted string or command. Indentation then changes inside the literal, including on repeated runs.

commits.title: Expand format ranges to cover whole multiline literals

fix.why_together: One commit on upstream master combines the formatter change and its regression tests. The dogfood merge has exactly that tree and also retains the earlier 1.11.1 backport in its history.

tests: CLI --lines=4:4 on the multiline-string example in issue #260
validation.detail: 12,927 assertions passed and 16 were marked broken. All 52 range-formatting checks passed. Unpatched master added four spaces to the selected string line. The merge preserved the file byte-for-byte. Tested dogfood commit 2d4fd57f7d7b47e9c35d6495c28cf3e39aa3d580.
11,964 assertions passed and 16 pre-existing assertions were marked broken. All 47 --lines checks passed. Tested dogfood commit 3efa0c13d1a3b33b7686d97b27b6ed3d017f674a.

draft.title: Formatting one line inside a multiline literal changes its value
draft.body:
Save this file as `literal.jl` using the indentation shown.

```julia
begin
    s = """
    a
    b
    c
    """
end
```

Run `runic --lines=4:4 --diff literal.jl` with unpatched Runic 1.11.1 or upstream master at `d65f5485e`. Only the line containing `b` gains indentation. Applying the edit changes the value of `s`, and formatting the same line again shifts it further. The expected diff for this file is empty.

Expand a selected range to the boundaries of any enclosing multiline string or command before inserting formatting markers. This keeps markers outside literal contents. Upstream issue #260 tracks the behavior.
